title: A Lantern for the Clock
premise: In 1917, in a snowbound river town cut off by the seasonal closing of its only bridge, battlefield nurse Orsen Thornbury keeps a private ledger of soldiers whose deaths the officers have erased or misreported. When a grieving mother arrives asking after a son officially listed as 'returned to duty,' Orsen realizes her ledger is the only honest record that exists — and that the garrison commander will burn it rather than let it reach the war office. With the help of a lamplighter, a disgraced chaplain, and the town's ferry widow, she smuggles the ledger past three checkpoints, discovering along the way that loyalty to people must sometimes outweigh obedience to institutions. The book ends with Orsen crossing the frozen river on foot, ledger intact, choosing to testify — and finding that the found family she built in the town crosses back over the ice with her.
about_author: Yara Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing military correspondence from the First World War, where she first encountered the small, stubborn records kept by ordinary people against official histories. She writes historical fiction about the quiet rebels whose names never made the dispatches.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In the military hospital at Marlow's Bend, Orsen finishes another night shift and adds three names to her hidden ledger of men the officers have written out of existence. She tells herself history happens elsewhere; the bridge closes tomorrow for the season. Emotional beat: the comfort and danger of secret witness.

chapters.title: Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the bridge's final day, she watches supply wagons and one last mail coach cross, hesitating over whether to send her ledger with them. A letter from a stranger — a mother named Ada Quill asking about her son — arrives too late to answer by post. Emotional beat: the door closing on safety.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ada Quill refuses to accept that Private Edmund Quill was 'returned to duty'; Orsen recognizes the name from her own pages. She cannot tell Ada the truth without exposing the ledger. Lamplighter Tam Beckett notices her distress and offers help without knowing why. Emotional beat: guilt crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Chaplain Confessed
chapters.summary: Chaplain Elias Wrenn's POV. Disgraced for questioning casualty reports, Wrenn reveals he has seen the officer's true ledgers: Edmund died in a retreat the command covered up. He warns Orsen that Commander Halsey audits all outgoing post now. Emotional beat: two keepers of secrets deciding to become keepers of truth.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen maps the gauntlet: the hospital gate, the telegraph office, and the bridgehead guardhouse, each searched for unauthorized papers. Ferry widow Marta Ostrova proposes an old smuggler's route across the ice — if it holds. Emotional beat: fear transformed into planning, the found family assembling.

chapters.title: A Copy in Candlelight
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam transcribes the ledger by lantern light while Orsen copies names onto ration cards and hymnal flyleaves. Ada, learning the truth about her son, chooses to stay and help rather than grieve alone. Halsey announces an inspection of all quarters. Emotional beat: grief converted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Inspection
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Halsey searches the nurses' quarters; the original ledger sits beneath floorboards as his boots pass overhead. Orsen realizes he already suspects someone is keeping records — a clerk was caught burning pages last week. Emotional beat: terror, and the discovery that she is not the only one who resisted.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Telegraph
chapters.summary: Wrenn's POV. Their plan to wire coded names to a war office contact fails when a sympathetic operator is arrested. Wrenn offers himself as decoy and is taken, buying the others a night. Orsen must decide whether the mission is worth the cost to people she loves. Emotional beat: the price of truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Over the Ice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax. With Halsey's patrols sweeping the town, Orsen, Tam, Marta, and Ada set out across the frozen river at night, the ledger sewn into Ada's coat. Ice cracks; a patrol lantern sweeps the shore; they hide in a reed bank until dawn. Emotional beat: courage at its thinnest margin.

chapters.title: A Lantern for the Clock
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Resolution. They reach the far rail depot as the bridge reopens; Orsen mails the ledger and gives testimony under her own name, ending her invisibility. Wrenn is released; Halsey is investigated. Ada plants a lantern by the river for every name in the book. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and family chosen, not given.
